title: Building the platform for agent coordination — Tom Moor, Linear
talk_summary: Tom Moor describes Linear's pragmatic AI journey and their new agent platform where agents are first-class users with identity, audit trails, OAuth install, and webhooks. He closes with concrete best practices for agent behavior in shared work surfaces: fast acknowledgment, plan-before-acting, natural thread behavior, and concise value-adding output.

takeaways.technique: Agents as first-class users with identity and audit trail
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents get identity, history, full audit trail of events, OAuth install, admin-managed access, and granular scopes (mentionable/assignable) so they behave like teammates in the same work surface as humans.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in linear agents are first class users um they have identity they have history you can see everything they do there's a full audit trail

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents form a plan before doing anything, communicate it up front, and get clarification before executing rather than attempting one-shots.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they'll form a plan um before doing anything um and communicate that plan up front and get clarification on it

takeaways.technique: Fast precise acknowledgment that mirrors the request
takeaways.what_they_do: On trigger, respond immediately (often emoji reaction) and reply in a way that restates the specific request to reassure the user the agent understood.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it should respond as fast as possible... the response should be like something I will produce a PR for for this specific thing you asked me

takeaways.what_they_do: If a human replies in a thread the agent started, the agent responds automatically without needing to be mentioned again, matching human teammate expectations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if somebody triggered you and then they replied in that thread, you shouldn't need to mention the agent again to get a response

takeaways.technique: Concise, value-adding output; no text splats
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly forbid dumping raw LLM text into comments/issues; require concise, useful, teammate-like output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LLMs, they they love to just produce tons of text. We don't want to see splats straight out of OpenAI into comments

takeaways.technique: Status discipline: move work to in-progress
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are expected to move the issue to in-progress when working, not leave it in backlog, mirroring human teammate norms.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're working on an issue, you should move that issue to in progress. Don't just leave it in the backlog
